clue.text: Does it need two hands to eat?

definitions.text: Does it need two hands to eat?

parts.words: Does it need two hands to eat?
parts.note: read as a fruit whose name is two animal hands, one paw after another, rather than a question about table manners

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether some awkward food has to be held in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical fruit's name is a doubled word for an animal's foot, so the clue's two hands describe it.

clue.text: Swimmer's half-heartedly feeble balance

indicators.note: half of the heart, one of the two middle letters, is taken out of the word for feeble

parts.note: feeble means poor
balance or composure means poise

explanation.surface: Someone's swimming stroke is described as weak and lacking poise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two middle Os of POOR, leaving POR.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine mammal that swims, so a swimmer by example.

clue.text: Throw away middle part of speech

indicators.note: of speech says the word is spoken, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: the middle part of the body is the waist

explanation.surface: An instruction to discard the central portion of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of speech' looks like a grammar term, but 'middle part' is the waist and 'of speech' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To waste something is to squander or throw it away.

clue.text: She's right in the middle of heavenly food

indicators.note: only the very centre of the word for heavenly food is kept, its first and last letters going

parts.note: manna is the food sent from heaven to the Israelites

explanation.surface: A woman is placed at the heart of some divine nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a woman's name, so 'she' stands for it as a crossword example.

clue.text: So to comprehend lama's reincarnation needs a bit of brain

indicators.note: to comprehend in its old sense of include or enclose, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: a reincarnation brings the lama back in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tibetan monk; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A Buddhist teaching: understanding the rebirth of a lama demands some brainpower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to comprehend' is used in its old sense of include, not understand, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The thalamus is a structure deep in the brain, a part of it.

clue.text: Sank putt, we hear, last

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a golfer who sinks a putt has holed out

explanation.surface: A golf commentator reports the final putt going in.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out is to last or endure under pressure.

clue.text: City state of mind produces sad expression

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the city
mentation is mental activity, a state of mind

explanation.surface: Some city's mood gives rise to a gloomy face.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamentation is an expression of grief or sorrow.

clue.text: Fail to change tack, but governess is not sacked

parts.note: a governess was addressed as Miss
someone who is not sacked stays in the job

explanation.surface: A nautical failure, yet the governess keeps her post.
explanation.walkthrough: In sailing, a ship that misses stays fails to come about when tacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing term for a vessel that fails to go about from one tack to the other.

clue.text: Depressed students over range of knowledge required

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain
ken is one's range of knowledge

explanation.surface: Students feel low after being set too much to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken means lowered or hollowed, a synonym of depressed in its physical sense.

clue.text: Failed to move away

indicators.note: moving the letters about rearranges them

explanation.surface: An attempt to relocate somewhere fell through.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means far off or away from home.

clue.text: Bitter delivered again, one quarter empty?

parts.note: something sent again is re-sent
the word full with one of its four letters gone is one quarter empty

explanation.surface: A drinker's pint of bitter is redelivered because it was not filled to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter here is beer in the surface, but the definition is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resentful feels bitter about an injustice.

clue.text: People trap very small particle

indicators.note: one word traps the other inside it

parts.note: people means men
very means so

explanation.surface: A crowd catches a tiny speck.
explanation.definitionFit: A meson is a subatomic particle, so a very small one.

clue.text: So happy those Apollo chose walked here?

definitions.meaning: the astronauts picked for the Apollo missions walked on the lunar surface, which is literally above the earth's satellite

explanation.surface: The astronauts selected for the Apollo programme were thrilled about where they walked.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for delighted, and literally the place the Apollo astronauts went.

clue.text: Film long sought by British intelligence

definitions.meaning: a 1949 film noir set in Vienna
the unknown further member of the Cambridge spy ring after Burgess and Maclean, hunted for years

explanation.surface: A movie about what British spies spent years looking for.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the classic Carol Reed film and the nickname for Kim Philby before his exposure.

clue.text: Girl has to beg

explanation.surface: A girl is forced to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, and a verb meaning to petition or plead for something.

clue.text: Singular criminal ends up having to hang

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A lone wrongdoer finishes on the gallows.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to hang it from above.

clue.text: Graduate wearing sort of scarlet is insufferable type

indicators.note: the anagram wears the graduate, taking it inside
sort of says a version of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate in a scarlet gown is an unbearable show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a graduate in a scarlet academic gown; 'wearing' means the anagram goes around the graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, a type others find insufferable.

clue.text: Emperor in Chinese dynasty shortly to accept sovereignty

indicators.note: the shortened word accepts the other inside it
shortly cuts off the last letter

parts.note: the Tang was a Chinese dynasty
the Raj was British sovereignty in India

explanation.surface: An emperor within a Chinese dynasty is soon to take power.
explanation.walkthrough: Trajan ruled Rome, not China: the Chinese dynasty is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor.

clue.text: Each part of chapter is intractable

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head
a verse is part of a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: Every section of a chapter proves stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means obstinately contrary, hence intractable.

clue.text: Plumber often wants it cleaner

definitions.meaning: a plumber often needs a small ring to seal a tap or joint

explanation.surface: A plumber frequently needs something to tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ring used in plumbing, and someone who washes things.

clue.text: Having eaten almost whole cake, room to recover

indicators.note: one word has eaten the other, holding it inside
almost drops the last letter

parts.note: an eclair is a whole cake

explanation.surface: After scoffing nearly an entire cake, someone needs space to recuperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ECLAIR to ECLAI, which RM eats: R + ECLAI + M.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to get it back, to recover it.

clue.text: Disputed a lot of lies?

parts.note: a tissue of lies is a whole web of falsehoods

explanation.surface: A claim challenged as just a pack of lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is one being argued over, in dispute.

clue.text: Approve of a dreadful mark being suppressed

indicators.note: the mark is held down inside the other word

parts.note: dreadful means dire
M is the abbreviation for the German mark

explanation.surface: Someone praises a terrible grade being hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire is to regard with approval.

clue.text: Fighting dissenting group, removing leader

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off

parts.note: a faction is a dissenting group within a larger body

explanation.surface: A breakaway group battles after ousting its chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is military combat, as in killed in action.

clue.text: Fail to attend court regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of court

explanation.surface: Someone keeps missing their appointments at court.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a class or meeting is to skip it deliberately.

clue.text: One who composed nasty letter took one month

parts.note: Peter Rachman was a notorious London slum landlord, one who let property
I is the Roman numeral one
Nov is November

explanation.surface: Someone wrote an unpleasant letter and it took them a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is one who lets property: Rachman was a 1950s London landlord whose name became a byword for exploitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachmaninov was a Russian composer.

clue.text: Some emotion at a lot of births

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lot of births stir up some feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is the adjective relating to birth.

clue.text: Saint in African country turned to this?

definitions.text: Saint in African country turned to this?

indicators.note: the saint goes in the other word
turned says the country's name is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A holy man in West Africa converted to a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses MALI to ILAM; S goes in after the I. Read whole, the clue describes conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion that West Africans, including those of Mali, have widely converted to.

clue.text: No strings attached to this performance

definitions.text: No strings attached to this performance

parts.words: No strings attached to this performance
parts.note: read literally: a show on an instrument that has no strings at all, mimed in the air

explanation.surface: A deal with no conditions on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming guitar playing without an instrument, so there are no strings.

clue.text: Embrace, dropping head right down? Horrible!

indicators.note: the first letter drops to the very bottom, the end of the word

parts.note: embrace means hug

explanation.surface: A hug where someone's head droops gives a cry of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugh is an exclamation of disgust, said of something horrible.

clue.text: Jack the Ripper, for example, in the Scrubs?

definitions.text: Jack the Ripper, for example, in the Scrubs?

parts.words: Jack the Ripper, for example, in the Scrubs?
parts.note: Jack the Ripper is an assumed title; in the Scrubs, a London prison, a name in jail would be a name in the nick

explanation.surface: A notorious murderer imagined serving time in Wormwood Scrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Wormwood Scrubs is a London prison, and nick is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper is an invented label for an unknown killer, an example of an informal name.

clue.text: Abandon supporters, almost

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter

parts.note: shelves support books and objects

explanation.surface: Someone nearly deserts their backers.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to set it aside, to abandon it.
